html:
The Dutch colony on Taiwan, run by the Dutch East India Company from 1624 to 1662. The map shows it in 1650, and keeps the label in 1700, by which time Qing China ruled the island.

The Company built Fort Zeelandia on a sandbar near modern Tainan, as a base for trade with Ming China and Japan and to block the Spanish and Portuguese. In 1642 it drove the Spanish from their posts in the north. The Dutch brought in Chinese settlers to grow sugar and rice and taxed them heavily; a large Chinese revolt in 1652 was crushed. Missionaries worked among the indigenous villages, while the Company fought those that resisted, such as the Kingdom of Middag.

In 1661 the Ming loyalist Koxinga landed with a large fleet and besieged Fort Zeelandia, and the Dutch surrendered in February 1662. Koxinga's family ruled the island as the Kingdom of Tungning until the Qing took it in 1683. Dutch rule had begun the large-scale Chinese settlement that shaped Taiwan.
sum: The Dutch colony on Taiwan, run by the Dutch East India Company from 1624 to 1662. The map shows it in 1650, and keeps the label in 1700, by which time Qing China ruled the island.
